question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(\frac{7}{9{x}^{7}}) & =\frac{7}{9}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}\frac{1}{{x}^{7}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the fact that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}\frac{1}{{x}^{7}}=-\infty .
$$

The positive factor of $\frac{7}{9}$ does not change the sign of the limit. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{7}{9}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}\frac{1}{{x}^{7}}=-\infty .
$$
